title: st.date_input: Error handling with invalid date entry
body:
### Summary

The [example for date_input](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/api-reference/widgets/st.date_input) fails with "This app has encountered an error. "

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the example for date_input
2. Type 0900/01/01 as date
3. Move the cursor between 0 and 9
4. Type anything (like 5 or . or -)

Is there a practical issue you are running into here? Pre-1500 or so (when the calendar was standardized to the Gregorian calendar), I'm not sure you can programmatically be doing a lot of data analysis in Python as the calendars were location-specific.

Ah, it's not about trying to use a really early date, but rather 
- having a year < 1000
- keeping the zero and typing another number

[USER] `date_input` wiget works correctly for all scenarious presented above, could you please confirm that this is an issue for the latest streamlit version?

The [example page for date_input](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/api-reference/widgets/st.date_input) uses the latest streamlit version (1.12.0), so it is still an issue, see [screencast](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25638902/190069960-eb1aca7d-35b5-4fed-a4e0-665760f709d1.webm).
